ops.body: A3.1 (d0f1e5c8) reviewed — NOT converged: 4 HIGH findings in the cost/classification control flow, A3.2 queued (release still blocked): (H1) committed-retry exception path double-counts the proposal (billed flag ignored by the generic branch); (H2) wall-deadline cancellation during post-propose work swallows the proposal cost entirely; (H3) max_usd is recorded but NOT ENFORCED during an infra retry chain — pre-commit infra failures can fund proposals past the cap (the enforce-vs-record distinction A6b's reservation math depends on); (H4) CandidateFault over-wraps the harness-side incumbent read-tree, contradicting failures.py's own docstring. Plus: per-line bytes-tolerant events reader (mid-UTF-8 tear kills read_text), schema-tolerant cost parsing, Measurement.produced = file-existence not exit-status. Confirmed sound by the same review: staged-retry structure (no re-propose after commit, no immutability bypass), aggregation formula, torn-line heal for ASCII writers, qwen3.5-9b entry (revisions + num_layers verified against upstream configs; price KeyError closes via A4.1's price entry). Sequencing: A4.1 (in flight) → A3.2 → targeted verify → release.
